slides.narration_text: Now we define what counts as a complete small teaching experience. The next idea is the core requirement, so slow down with it. Your five minutes need a stimulus or instruction, a scaffold, a learner Attempt, your Coaching, and a Renewed attempt. Without that second try, you have delivered a short lecture with a response in the middle. With it, you have evidence that your coaching changed what the learner could do next. One question, one sentence, or one short prompt can be enough.

slides.narration_text: You may be wondering what teaching format is allowed. Let’s look at the simplest answer: An interactive lecture is acceptable. You may lecture, provided you carry the room through one complete small cycle. That means your explanation cannot stay one-way all the way through. You still manage the purpose, the pace, and the learners’ attention, but at some point a response has to come back to you, and you have to use that response. The one-way lecture is not acceptable because it never lets the learner try, hear coaching, and try again. The format is flexible; the cycle is not.
